result.description:
Civil Engineer

Location: 17 Coolawanyah Road, Karratha WA 6714
Employment Type: Full-Time
Salary: AUD $95,000 – $100,000 per annum + Superannuation

About Our Client

Our client, Norwest Group, is a leading Western Australian company providing civil construction, transport, mining, logistics, and infrastructure services across the Pilbara and regional Western Australia. With a strong reputation for delivering quality projects safely and efficiently, Norwest Group continues to grow and is seeking an experienced Civil Engineer to join their team in Karratha, WA.

About the Role

As a Civil Engineer, you will play a key role in the planning, design, coordination, and delivery of civil construction and infrastructure projects. Working closely with project teams, you will ensure projects are completed safely, efficiently, within budget, and in accordance with engineering standards and project requirements.

Key Responsibilities
Plan and coordinate civil construction activities in accordance with project specifications, engineering standards, and quality requirements.
Prepare, review, and interpret engineering drawings, technical specifications, and construction documentation.
Coordinate site operations, including labour, plant, equipment, subcontractors, and material deliveries to ensure project milestones are achieved.
Conduct site investigations and assess geotechnical information to support safe and effective construction methods.
Prepare project cost estimates, quantity calculations, budgets, and assist with project cost control.
Monitor project progress and evaluate design changes, assessing their impact on project costs and timelines.
Perform engineering and structural analysis to ensure infrastructure meets safety, stability, and compliance requirements.
Assist in the design and development of roads, drainage systems, transport infrastructure, and other civil engineering works.
Liaise with clients, contractors, consultants, and project stakeholders throughout all stages of project delivery.
Ensure compliance with workplace health and safety requirements, environmental standards, and company policies.

Essential Requirements
Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering or a related discipline.
Minimum of three (3) years of relevant post-qualification experience.
Strong knowledge of civil engineering principles, construction methodologies, and Australian Standards.
Experience preparing engineering documentation, technical reports, and project cost estimates.
Ability to interpret engineering drawings and technical specifications.
Excellent communication, organisational, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a team.
Current Australian Driver's Licence or the ability to obtain one.

Desirable
Experience in civil construction, mining, transport, or infrastructure projects.
Knowledge of project planning, scheduling, and contract administration.
Experience using engineering design and project management software.


What Our Client Offers
Full-time permanent position.
Competitive salary of AUD $95,000 – $100,000 per annum + Superannuation.
Opportunity to work on diverse and exciting civil infrastructure projects.
Supportive and collaborative team environment.
Career development and professional growth opportunities.
A workplace committed to safety, quality, and continuous improvement.

result.description:
MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 






We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 






As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 






Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 






To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.




About Medical Oncology Services
 
The Medical Oncology Unit at Monash Health is among the largest in Australia. Offering a comprehensive range of services including inpatient care, outpatient support, chemotherapy infusion, and an extensive clinical trials program. This unit provides thorough cancer care across all types of tumors and medical disciplines. Guided by Monash Health's iCARE values --integrity, compassion, accountability, respect, and excellence-- the unit is dedicated to delivering best practices and superior management to benefit all patients. Key services include chemotherapy for all solid organ cancers, whether for curative or palliative purposes. Care is delivered at Moorabbin Hospital (including inpatient, outpatient, and infusion services) and at Monash Medical Centre (with clinical trials conducted at the Monash Health Translational Precinct - MHTP and inpatient care). 
 
A Day in the Life
- The position offers a part-time Fixed Term consulting position at one location 
- Specialisation in Breast & Gynaecology Cancers is required
 
The ideal candidate will be enthusiastic and demonstrate a strong ability to collaborate effectively within a dynamic and ever-changing environment. They should be capable of not only adapting to change but also leading and driving it within the team. The oncologist will play a key role in both inpatient and outpatient oncology care as per the agreed roster. 
Responsibilities will also include mentoring, supervising, and managing the performance of oncology registrars and fellows, as well as handling other relevant non-clinical duties. Additionally, the oncologist will support the Director and Deputy Director of Oncology in ongoing service development efforts. 
 
About You
 
You are a dynamic medical professional, described as enthusiastic and motivated to perform at your best every day, you demonstrate excellent communication and interpersonal skills. 
 
What you need: 
 
Registration with the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA) 
Appropriate health professional tertiary qualifications 
Fellowship of the Royal Australian College of Physicians 
Demonstrable relevant knowledge and experience in the management of oncological disease 
Experience in oncology clinical trials 
Meets Monash Health requirements for credentialing and scope of practice in oncology 
Experience in teaching and involvement in research 
Experience in writing project applications and supervising project plans 
Credentialing and Scope of Practice: 
As part of the application process, the incumbent must submit their credentials using CGOV 
 


For a confidential discussion and to explore this opportunity further, please reach out to Zee Wan Wong, Director of Oncology or Sarah Mwaba, Senior Administration Assistant on 0448 709 673



Position Description can be found here





Our Culture and Values 






At Monash Health, our people are at the heart of everything we do. Our culture is inclusive, supportive and future-focused, underpinned by clear values and a commitment to continuous improvement. 







Our teams play a critical role in bringing our new strategy to life, challenging traditional approaches, embracing innovation, and ensuring every appointment reflects our commitment to equity, transparency and excellence. 







You'll be encouraged to share ideas, contribute to improvement initiatives, and grow alongside experienced professionals who are passionate about what they do. 







We are Full Hearted, Open Minded and All In, enabling excellent service delivery and a positive candidate and employee experience every time. 







We recognise the value of equal employment opportunity. We are committed to patient safety, promoting fairness, equity and diversity in the workplace and to Child Safe Standards. 





How to Apply


Applications are accepted via the Monash Health online EHub system. For information including how to apply and probity check requirements, please click here for the 'Application Guide'


Applications will be screened upon receipt and selection activity may commence prior to the closing date. 


Applications close: 21 July 2026    Click here to Apply now →
